title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 164 (Bailor's responsibility to bailee)

content.overview: Section 164 provides that the bailor is responsible to the bailee for any loss which the bailee may sustain by reason that the bailor was not entitled to make the bailment, or to receive back the goods, or to give directions respecting them.
content.glance: Bailor is responsible to the bailee for loss sustained because the bailor was not entitled to make the bailment, receive back the goods, or give directions respecting them.
content.study: The bailor is responsible to the bailee for any loss which the bailee may sustain by reason that the bailor was not entitled to make the bailment, or to receive back the goods, or to give directions respecting them. Current-law framing: protects the bailee who acts on the bailor's apparent authority or title.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: The bailor is responsible to the bailee for any loss which the bailee may sustain by reason that the bailor was not entitled to make the bailment, or to receive back the goods, or to give directions respecting them.

examples.title: Bailor without title
examples.body: Bailor bails goods he is not entitled to bail. Bailee suffers loss as a result. Bailor is responsible under Section 164.

hypotheticals.question: Bailee suffers loss because the bailor was not entitled to make the bailment. Is the bailor responsible?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 164 makes the bailor responsible for such loss.
